description:
crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:171-182

    /// Per-creation success entry in an [`EmailImportResponse`] (RFC 8621 §4.8).
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct EmailImportCreated {
        pub id: Id,
        pub blob_id: Id,
        pub thread_id: Id,
        pub size: u64,
    }

Both sibling types in the same module ARE #[non_exhaustive]:

  EmailImportResponse  line 185  #[non_exhaustive]
  EmailParseResponse   line 239  #[non_exhaustive]

EmailImportCreated is the per-creation success entry for a created Email — RFC 8621 §4.8 could conceivably grow new fields (the spec is silent on whether the created-map entry shape is closed), and JMAP extensions could add per-server fields. Without #[non_exhaustive], adding even one new field is a breaking change in the next 0.1.x — which contradicts the 'pre-publish readiness sweep' goal of this epic.

JMAP-sc1b.47 already filed (and closed) the same finding for 12 greenfield Property enums missing #[non_exhaustive]. This one slipped through because it landed in commit 72fc913 (feat(mail-client): add typed Email/import and Email/parse methods, 2026-05-10) AFTER the .47 sweep.

Fix: prepend #[non_exhaustive] before the #[derive] line. Cookie-cutter propagation rule: jmap-mail-client is canonical for the extension-client family, so any newly-added response struct here must carry #[non_exhaustive] before sibling crates copy the pattern.
title: P2: EmailImportCreated lacks #[non_exhaustive] while EmailImportResponse and EmailParseResponse in the same module have it
